extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and writers interested in Jorge Luis Borges, literary technique, and creative-writing influenced by Borges
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing literature in the manner or spirit of Jorge Luis Borges: concise, philosophically-inflected short fiction that balances universal themes with local materials and intertextual play. Useful for writers aiming to adopt Borgesian methods and for critics assessing such work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precursors and revision of literary past
rubrics_metrics.description: “Every writer creates his own precursors. His work modifies our conception of the past, as it will modify the future.” (the word 'precursor' should be cleansed of connotation of polemics or rivalry.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with predecessors not as rivals but as materials to be reinterpreted; a work should be judged on how it reshapes our view of earlier literature. Anti-pattern: treating precursors only as targets to be defeated or dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid limiting literature to 'local colour' / cultural nationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges denies that Argentine literature should distinguish itself by limiting itself to 'local colour', which he equates with cultural nationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make national identity the sole defining feature of work; you may write about local themes but avoid reducing literature to mere regional exoticism or a nationalist stance. Example: write about gauchos or tangos without framing them as curiosities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins as opportunity for innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: “The very fact of writing from the margins provides Argentine writers with a special opportunity to innovate without being bound to the canons of the centre ... at once a part of and apart from the centre, which gives them much potential freedom.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a peripheral or marginal position to experiment and break canonical constraints rather than to mimic or inwardly deflect. Valued work shows inventive approaches enabled by not being bound to centre norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance universal themes with local grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges focused on universal themes, but also composed a substantial body of literature on themes from Argentine folklore and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for work that addresses universal/philosophical questions while drawing on local history or folklore; avoid pandering to readers or exoticizing local culture. Example: integrate Martín Fierro material without reducing it to mere 'local colour.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate aesthetic from moral evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In his essays Borges separates his admiration for the aesthetic virtues of a work from his mixed opinion of the moral virtues of its protagonist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing fiction, distinguish artistic/aesthetic merit (style, formal invention) from moral judgments about characters or actions. Anti-pattern: collapsing aesthetic assessment into moral approval or condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show philosophical systems by immersive worldbuilding
rubrics_metrics.description: “One of his methods consists of adopting the premises of a given philosophical system and recreating the universe as its adherents perceive it.” Example: in Tlön, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius Borges illustrates philosophical idealism by presenting a world whose inhabitants conceive reality as a product of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed philosophical ideas by having the fictional world instantiate them; let readers experience the consequences of a philosophical premise through plot and setting rather than through explicit exposition. Anti-pattern: heavy-handed didactic explanation of abstract doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present ideas experientially; emphasize the vivid and marvelous
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophical ideas in his texts appear so that readers experience them before conceptualizing them, emphasizing what is vivid and marvelous and appealing to intuition rather than to conceptual argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sensory, imagistic, or narrative instantiation of concepts so that the reader perceives their effects directly. Scoring note: writing that makes an idea felt (not just explained) is stronger in this mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive world details logically from premises (internal consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of Borges's fictional worlds follow logically from their premises (e.g., Tlön's languages lack nouns because its inhabitants do not conceive of 'things').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building speculative settings or systems, ensure that specific features coherently follow from the core premise. Anti-pattern: arbitrary details that contradict or ignore the world’s stated logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aestheticism: value beauty over doctrinal truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges had a consistent tendency to 'value religious or philosophical ideas for their aesthetic worth and even for what they contain of the singular and the marvelous.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and shape thematic material for its imaginative and aesthetic resonance rather than for its philosophical correctness or doctrinal fidelity. Works judged by this criterion are valued for their imaginative power and beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form selection aligned with personal strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges's blindness led him to favour poetry and shorter narratives over novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose forms (poetry, short stories, novellas) that suit the writer's abilities, constraints, and artistic aims. Practical guidance: favor brevity or condensed forms if they better serve concentration, clarity, or production conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic transparency and naturalism over baroque excess
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges's later style is far more transparent and naturalistic than his earlier works; his work progressed away from what he referred to as 'the baroque.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for clarity and controlled language rather than ornate verbosity; value precision and translucency in prose. Anti-pattern: gratuitous ornamentation that obscures meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate interdisciplinary concepts elegantly into fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges used mathematical and philosophical concepts (e.g., set theory in 'The Book of Sand') with elegance in his stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating technical or scholarly ideas, weave them organically into narrative so they illuminate theme and plot without becoming overtly didactic. Example: use mathematical metaphors or structures to enrich, not to lecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertextual play and pseudo-translations as artistic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges sometimes presented imitations as translations (e.g., imitations of Swedenborg), using intertextual hoaxes and forged attributions as part of his literary technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ intertextual games, fictional documents, and playful authorship to destabilize notions of authority and originality — but do so with clear artistic purpose. Anti-pattern: such devices used gratuitously without thematic justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide multilingual and multicultural reading enriches writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges was immersed in Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Anglo-Saxon and Old Norse literature, and read translations from Near and Far Eastern works; his cosmopolitan reading informed his fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate broad reading across languages and traditions to supply material, perspectives, and formal strategies. This breadth supports intertextual depth and cosmopolitan outlook in creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use art/media to relate emotionally and socially to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Borges represented a humanist view of media that stressed the social aspect of art driven by emotion and was more interested in how the tool could be used to relate to people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make choices (tone, form, medium) aimed at creating emotional or social connection; prioritize the readerly experience and relational effects of the work. Scoring note: successful pieces create palpable emotional resonance or social commentary through form and voice.
